name: Bill Ackman
style: Owns a handful of simple, cash rich, dominant companies and sometimes pushes management for change.
why_follow: The book is only about 14 stocks, so each new name is a high conviction bet worth studying. Caveat: Pershing often discloses new stakes in its own letters before the 13F, and some buys (Intercontinental Exchange, Alcon) came after June 30, so the 13F already lags.

bought.name: Netflix
bought.note: New stake, about 13.1 million shares, about 4.9% of the portfolio.

bought.name: Uber
bought.note: Up about 15% to about 34.3 million shares. Now the largest position.

sold.name: Alphabet
sold.note: Reported as fully sold. Pershing had already cut most of it in Q1.

sold.name: Amazon
sold.note: Reported cut of about 25%. One tracker disagrees.

view: In a June 1, 2026 interview he said he is finding 'a lot of really cheap stocks in a market that's hitting new highs', because AI and chip enthusiasm has left other strong companies, such as Meta, Microsoft and Amazon, undervalued.

name: Warren Buffett
style: Buys great businesses with durable moats at fair prices and holds them for years.
why_follow: Berkshire moves slowly and with huge size, so a new or bigger stake is a strong long term signal. Caveat: Greg Abel became CEO at the start of 2026, so recent trades may be his calls, not Buffett's, and the 13F leaves out Berkshire's record cash pile and its private deals.

bought.note: Stake up about 44% to more than 57 million shares, about $5.4 billion.

name: Ray Dalio
style: Global macro: bets on growth, inflation and interest rates across countries, balanced so no single season can sink the whole book.
why_follow: Bridgewater is one of the world's largest hedge funds and Dalio's cycle framework drives the cycle block on this dashboard. Caveat: its 13F is mostly S&P 500 index ETFs; its real bets are bonds, currencies and futures that 13Fs do not show. Dalio also no longer runs the firm day to day.

name: Stanley Druckenmiller
style: Top down macro trader: finds the big trend, bets hard when the odds look best, and cuts fast when wrong.
why_follow: He has one of the best long records in macro, and his stock picks often lead big themes. Caveat: he trades fast, so a 13F that is six weeks old may already be stale, and his currency, bond and commodity bets do not show up. Several weights below include call options.

name: David Tepper
style: Opportunistic: buys hard when others panic, rides the Fed, and makes big concentrated bets on tech and China.
why_follow: He is one of the best at buying fear, and his moves often show where a big money manager sees value. Caveat: the 13F hides his bonds, credit and short positions, and he trades often.

name: Cathie Wood
style: Buys fast growing disruptive tech (AI, robotics, genomics, crypto, space) and holds through big swings.
why_follow: ARK publishes its ETF trades every day, so you can see buys and sells within a day instead of waiting for the 13F. Caveat: her picks are high risk and volatile, and rising rates hurt this style the most.
